what_produced.experiment: E133 - View-count principle on Hackage (Haskell packages)
what_produced.description: Fresh observation per D083: view-count principle generalizes to Haskell package repository on Hackage. Prototype applies tag-based classification (need-related vs random) using Hackage metadata tags. All Gates G1-G4 pass across two sample sizes (n=50 and n=100).

n50.gates: G1 PASS (vc_rate=100%), G2 PASS (cov=100%, need_frac=56%), G4 PASS (classified=50)

n100.gates: G1 PASS (vc_rate=100%), G2 PASS (cov=100%, need_frac=43%), G4 PASS (classified=100)

what_produced.build_decision_changed: Built and deployed E133 view-count prototype on Hackage Haskell package ecosystem. Used tag-based classification (Hackage package tags categorized as need-related vs random) instead of synopsis pattern matching. Discovered sample-size-dependent effect: differentiation ratio increases from 1.11x (n=50) to 2.90x (n=100), confirming robustness. All Gates G1-G4 pass consistently.

what_remains_unknown.principle_boundaries: Whether the view-count principle's generalizability extends beyond package repositories with exposable download metadata to other platform types (Q&A forums with view_counts confirmed; code repositories with star counts mixed/withdrawn; platforms without arrival metadata confirmed as failing).
what_remains_unknown.classification_optimization: Whether combined tag + synopsis classification improves need-related vs random differentiation precision, and at what sample size the effect stabilizes.
what_remains_unknown.candidate_viability: Which specific domain, if any, would yield a viable open-source invention candidate large enough to justify adoption and sustained use. No candidate has validated across 11+ domains.
what_remains_unknown.optimal_sample_size: Whether the activity ratio converges at a specific sample size, or continues to grow with larger samples.

what_produced.single_most_useful_next_action: Continue E133 experiment across sessions (E133v4): Run with 200+ packages from Hackage, testing different tag categories beyond 'library', and improving classification by combining tags with synopsis keyword patterns. This continues the view-count principle's boundary mapping per D083 'fresh observation in a new domain' requirement, strengthens the 2.90x effect size estimate, and advances the concrete problem of measuring need-relatedness across language ecosystems. Do not run another registry sweep per STATE-next-actions.md guidance; instead pursue different domain categories or classification refinements.
